problem: Streaming VLN agents either stop-and-think (perceptual blindness) or store all frames and sample uniformly or heuristically, which pollutes the context with redundant frames. Open-loop imitation and naive DAgger-style correction data also suffer compounding errors and contaminated data once the agent drifts far from the path.
motivation: Long-horizon navigation needs a compact, information-dense memory and the ability to recover from deviations. Uniform sampling picks up task-irrelevant frames such as walls and corners, and larger K makes it worse. Correction data collected after large deviations no longer matches the instruction.
key_idea: Select memory frames online by maximizing a unified score of instruction relevance, visual diversity and temporal coverage, and collect corrective state-action pairs only within a geodesic-distance trust region around the expert path.
insight: Content-aware memory matters more than a longer memory: with uniform sampling, performance drops as K grows past 8, while AMR keeps a dense context (AMR alone: SR 47.3->50.9). Restricting correction data to a geodesic trust region (tau=3) beats vanilla DAgger at the same data scale (180K: SR 56.3 vs 54.8) and roughly matches DAgger with 240K samples (SR 56.0). Too small a tau gives a conservative policy (SR 53.7 at tau=1), and too large a tau adds low-quality data.
method: Observation/reasoning decoupling: the agent perceives continuously while acting, keeps a fixed-size VRAM-resident memory bank of K=8 frames, and takes the instruction, the memory and the last 4 frames as input to predict an action chunk of 4 actions.
Adaptive Memory Refinement (AMR): greedily picks frames from a candidate pool by maximizing lambda_R*Sem - (1-lambda_R)*(w_V*Vis + w_T*Temp), with w_V+w_T=1.
Semantic relevance: cosine similarity between the VLM text embedding of the instruction and the frame embedding from the visual encoder plus projector.
Visual diversity and temporal coverage: the visual penalty is the max cosine similarity to any memory frame, and the temporal penalty is 1/(min |t_f - t_m| + eps).

Corrective fine-tuning: roll out the SFT policy, compute the deviation DM(s_t) as the minimum geodesic distance to the expert path, and if 0<DM<=tau (tau=3) query the Habitat ShortestPathFollower for the expert action and store (state, action, frame). Abort the episode when DM>tau.

Training recipe: SFT on about 360K samples (R2R-CE, R2R-EnvDrop, RxR-CE) with stochastic action offsets, image augmentation and LLM-rewritten reverse instructions, then about 180K corrective samples mixed with LLaVA-Video-178K to limit forgetting.
Real-world deployment: a Unitree GO2 streams video to an RTX 4090 server, and the onboard controller converts each 4-action chunk into a single relative pose (dx, dy, dtheta).

setting.training_data: About 360K SFT samples from R2R-CE, R2R-EnvDrop and RxR-CE, with augmentation and reverse instructions; about 180K corrective state-action samples from Habitat SPF; LLaVA-Video-178K for regularization. No ScaleVLN.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB only (no depth, odometry or panorama)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions: forward 25 cm, turn left 15°, turn right 15°, stop, predicted as chunks of 4
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes), plus a real Unitree GO2 quadruped
setting.privileged: none at test time (the expert shortest-path follower is used only during training data collection)

numbers.extra: RGB only; no ScaleVLN; SFT + corrective fine-tuning

results: With RGB only, DecoVLN reaches SR 56.3 / SPL 50.5 on R2R-CE and SR 54.2 / SPL 46.3 on RxR-CE val-unseen. It beats StreamVLN (52.8/47.2 and 48.6/42.5) and NaVILA (54.0/49.0 on R2R-CE), without ScaleVLN data. The appendix shows StreamVLN with RGB+Depth is still slightly better on R2R (SR 56.9) but worse on RxR.
limitations: The 7B model cannot run onboard, so the real robot depends on a remote GPU server with network latency.
There is no deep recovery mechanism when landmarks vanish or perceptual aliasing occurs, and real-world results are qualitative only.
The long-horizon results appear only in a figure, and the hyperparameters lambda_R, w_V and w_T are hand-tuned.
